prompt: A right triangle has vertices at $(0, 0), (6, 0), (0, 4)$. Find its area.
hint: Two sides of this triangle lie on the axes and meet in a right angle. Those two sides can be the base and the height.

hints.title: 🔁 Another angle
hints.text: Picture the rectangle with corners $(0, 0)$, $(6, 0)$, $(6, 4)$ and $(0, 4)$. The triangle is exactly half of that rectangle.
Two sides of this triangle lie on the axes and meet in a right angle. Those two sides can be the base and the height.
The side on the $x$-axis has length $6$ and the side on the $y$-axis has length $4$. Find half of $6 \times 4$.
$\frac{1}{2} \times 6 \times 4 = 12$, so the area of the triangle is $12$ square units.

explanation: The side from $(0, 0)$ to $(6, 0)$ lies on the $x$-axis, so use it as the base with length $6$.
The side from $(0, 0)$ to $(0, 4)$ goes straight up the $y$-axis, so the height is $4$.
The base and height meet at a right angle, so the formula $A = \frac{1}{2}bh$ applies: $\frac{1}{2}(6)(4)$.
Half of $24$ is $12$, so the area of the triangle is $12$ square units.
